records.title: OpenAI Codex: Windows: nested-quote corruption in pwsh -Command exec_command (200+ failures across 0.148/0.150) + file-read tool rejects workspace files
records.content: ## Environment Windows 11; codex CLI 0.148.0 and 0.150.1 (both affected); PowerShell 7 as default shell; project AGENTS.md asks for UTF-8 console encoding, so many commands start with `[Console]::OutputEncoding=...` preambles. ## Issue A: pwsh `-Command` nested-quote corruption in exec_command Across three days of session rollouts we counted 26 / 15 / 209 occurrences of `exec_command failed`, all with the same corruption shape — quotes inside the command body get mangled so PowerShell sees interleaved broken quoting: Intended (model-generated): ``` pwsh -Command "$env:FORCE_COLOR='0'; ..." ``` As executed (from session log, verbatim): ``` pwsh.exe -Command '$env:FORCE_COLOR='"'0'; ... ``` Typical patterns: `'"'0'`, `foreach("'$p`, `'"'{0}"'` -f ...`` — single/double quotes interleaved in ways that can never parse. Failures cluster during heavy multi-file review turns where many long one-liner PowerShell text-processing commands are issued; they occur on both 0.148.0 and 0.150.1 and with multiple model tiers, so it does not look like a single model or single version regression. When the same work is expressed as a script file or simpler commands, it succeeds. Questions / asks: - Where is the boundary where these commands get re-serialized (model tool output → shell invocation)? records.title: OpenAI Codex: [ChatGPT Work] Conversation-length limit blocks recoverable closeout and handoff
records.content: ## Summary When a long-running ChatGPT Work conversation reaches its maximum length, the conversation becomes unusable before it can produce a reliable closeout or handoff. The replacement conversation may not know which final instruction was processed, which was not, or whether an external side effect completed. This is distinct from ordinary context compaction or CLI token-window rollover: the UI hard-blocks further work in the conversation. ## Environment - ChatGPT Work on the web - Long-running, tool-heavy project conversation - Connected GitHub, email, and scheduled-task actions - Multiple external side effects and approval gates - Observed 2026-08-29 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Use a ChatGPT Work conversation for a long-running project with connected-service actions. 2. Complete multiple repository and deployment operations over many turns. 3. Send a final instruction that creates or updates an external automation. 4. Reach the conversation-length limit immediately afterward. 5. Start a replacement conversation using the available history/summary. 6. Try to determine whether that final instruction ran. 7. Reconcile live GitHub, email, and automation state manually. ## Actual behavior - The capacity warning appears only after the conversation is no longer usable. - No reserved closeout mode remains available. - The handoff does not reliably identify the last processed instruction and the first unprocessed instruction. - The replacement lacks an authoritative action receipt for the final connected-service mutation. - Exact roles, ordering, links, unresolved approvals, and pending inputs are not preserved as a structured handoff. - Manual provider-by-provider reconciliation is required. In the observed case, the final automation-creation instruction actually completed, but the exhausted conversation never returned a visible completion response. The replacement reasonably treated it as potentially unhandled and created an equivalent duplicate before later live-state

records.title: OpenAI Codex: TUI: allow configuring or disabling the inline diff preview limit
records.content: ### What variant of Codex are you using? Codex CLI 0.151.0 ### What feature would you like to see? Please add a TUI setting that controls the maximum number of rows shown in rich inline diff previews, including an unlimited option. For example: ```toml [tui] diff_preview_max_rows = 0 # unlimited ``` The current rich inline renderer limits patch previews to 12 rendered rows and then shows: ```text … Diff preview limited (ctrl + t to view transcript). ``` That default is sensible for many users, but some users prefer to inspect every edit as it happens without repeatedly opening and closing the Ctrl+T transcript overlay. Suggested behavior: - Preserve the current limit as the default. - Allow a positive integer to select a custom preview size. - Allow `0` (or an explicit `unlimited` value) to render the complete rich diff inline. ### Why the existing alternatives do not cover this - Ctrl+T requires switching into the transcript overlay whenever a patch is applied. - `/diff` is an on-demand repository-wide view rather than an automatic per-edit preview. - `tui.raw_output_mode = true` displays complete patch content, but changes the entire transcript to plain, copy-friendly rendering. It is not a diff-specific preference and loses the rich inline presentation. - `--no-alt-screen` preserves terminal scrollback but does not change the diff preview limit. This would let users retain syntax-highlighted/rich TUI output while opting into complete inline diffs. The setting would remain opt-in, so large diffs would not affect users who prefer the compact default. Related but distinct: #40220 requests display preferences for inline diff cards in the Codex App; this request concerns the Codex CLI TUI and specifically allowing more or unlimited rich preview rows.

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Document the Codex App's configuration surface and which parts are stable
records.content: ### What variant of Codex are you using? App (Codex Desktop, macOS) ### What feature would you like to see? Please document the Codex App's configuration and deployment surfaces, and state a compatibility contract for them. The CLI is open source and its configuration is documented. The App is not, and its configuration surface is effectively undiscoverable: the files it reads, where they live, their schemas, the deep links it accepts, and which of these are stable across releases. ## Why this matters - a concrete symptom Issue #18819 asks for a configurable SSH connect timeout in Codex Desktop. As far as I can tell that setting already exists; it simply is not documented anywhere, so users file requests for behavior that already ships, and maintainers spend attention on it. That is a documentation gap presenting as a feature gap, and I doubt it is the only instance. ## Use case We are deploying Codex App to a managed developer fleet. Devices are configured by MDM, and developers are not expected to hand-configure their tooling. To do that responsibly we need to know: 1. Which configuration files the App reads, where they are located, and their schemas, including anything intended for administrator or device-management use rather than end-user editing. 2. Which deep links (`codex://...`) are supported, and what each does. 3. How the App discovers and stores SSH remote connections and remote projects: what is read from `~/.ssh/config`, what is persisted in application state, and what the lifecycle is when a connection or project is removed. 4. A compatibility statement for each of the above - which are supported and stable, which are internal and may change without notice. Point 4 is the one that actually matters. We can discover behavior empirically; what we cannot do is know whether it will survive the next release. records.title: OpenAI Codex: Restore direct `codex resume <thread-id>` hint on exit, or make it configurable
records.content: ### What variant of Codex are you using? Codex CLI / TUI ### What feature would you like to see? PR #23234 changed the exit hint for named threads from: ```text To continue this session, run codex resume <thread-id> ``` to: ```text To continue this session, run codex resume, then select <thread-name> (<thread-id>) ``` I understand the motivation behind #23234: thread names are not necessarily unique, so suggesting `codex resume <thread-name>` directly would be ambiguous. However, the thread ID itself is unique, and Codex already supports: ```bash codex resume <thread-id> ``` For users who frequently resume sessions from terminal history, copy/paste, scripts, or multiple terminals, the previous hint was considerably more useful because it provided a directly executable command. The new behavior adds an unnecessary interactive step: ```text codex resume → open picker → locate/select thread ``` when the exact thread ID is already available at the time the exit message is generated. ### Suggested behavior Ideally, `/exit` should continue to display the direct UUID-based command even when the thread has a name: ```text To continue this session, run codex resume 01a04cab-3b3c-7ff3-9ca7-bac161xx41d5 ``` The thread name could optionally still be shown as additional context: ```text To continue "Alege domeniul pentru portal", run: codex resume 01a04cab-3b3c-7ff3-9ca7-bac161xx41d5 ``` This preserves both: - the human-readable thread name; - a deterministic, directly executable resume command. ### Alternative If the picker-based behavior is preferred as the default, it would be useful to make the exit hint configurable, for example: ```toml resume_hint = "direct" ``` versus: ```toml resume_hint = "picker" ``` ### Why this matters `codex resume <thread-id>` is: - deterministic; - non-interactive; - directly copy/pasteable; - shell-history friendly; - usable from scripts; - unaffected by duplicate thread names. records.content: ### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)? 26.825.41651 (build 7345) ### What subscription do you have? Pro ### What platform is your computer? records.title: OpenAI Codex: Add an in-session /resume command to Codex CLI
records.content: ## Problem Codex CLI can resume saved sessions with `codex resume SESSION_ID`, but only after exiting the active TUI. Claude Code supports `/resume` from within an active session, so users can switch to saved work without leaving the interface. This matters when someone starts a fresh session and then realizes they need to continue earlier work. ## Requested behavior - `/resume` opens the existing resume picker for the current workspace. - `/resume SESSION_ID` switches directly to the specified saved session. - The current session remains saved and can be resumed later. ## Context A similar request was raised in #4056, but it is closed and the feature is still unavailable in the current CLI.

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Support app targets in executor plugin hooks

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Respond to terminal queries from TTY subprocesses
records.content: Respond to terminal queries from TTY subprocesses ## Why Programs running in a PTY can block while waiting for replies to terminal queries. ## What changed - Intercept device-status, window-size, cursor-position, and DEC private-mode queries from TTY subprocess output and write bounded responses to the subprocess input. - Remove handled queries from the output stream while preserving other escape sequences and output, including queries split across chunks. - Apply the responder to both direct and driver-backed TTY process spawning. ## Testing Added tests for driver-backed query handling and for a PTY subprocess that waits for a cursor-position response before exiting. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: 9a150b525560b120be592c42e61256b6fc223aa170af983e4c1129bb1575d9a1 -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Run executor hooks for interrupted turns
records.content: Run executor hooks for interrupted turns ## Why Executor-scoped cleanup hooks need to observe an interrupted turn as well as a normally completed one. ## What changed - Allow bundled executor plugins to register the allowlisted `Interrupt` hook alongside `Stop`, while preserving multiple allowed hook entries from the selected executor environment. - Run interrupt hooks with the interrupted turn's last step discovery and turn metadata. Turns without a step context do not reuse discovery from an earlier turn. - Keep executor-scoped interrupt hooks asynchronous and omit public hook lifecycle events for them, matching executor `Stop` hook behavior. ## Testing Added coverage for hook filtering and registration, interrupt execution and metadata propagation, environment selection, and turns without a step context. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: b04fbab580c7b02e454b0e728993daca543e3a12c5ecdfbf88faf4ed81b4a6ec -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Preserve context baselines across nested agent forks
records.content: Preserve context baselines across nested agent forks ## What changed - Treat a surviving full world-state snapshot as a context baseline when a fork removes the associated user message. - Restore the previous turn settings and reference context from that baseline, without treating the segment as a user turn for rollback. - Ignore partial snapshots and full snapshots superseded by compaction. ## Testing - Cover resumed rollout reconstruction with removed task messages, partial snapshots, and compaction. - Verify nested agents inherit developer instructions and environment context exactly once across history modes and compacted histories. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: 4bd34e0e713ffe721b740314a3be66c34c30c4a2019a3e04506b68ea6fdf5e16 -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Add shared Guardian transcript collection
records.content: Add shared Guardian transcript collection ## What changed - Add a reusable transcript contributor for synchronous and asynchronous Guardian context, with borrowed conversation history and request-specific configuration. - Preserve conversation order and role or tool attribution while applying separate per-entry limits for messages, ordinary tools, and Node REPL-backed outputs. - Make tool calls, tool outputs, and reasoning independently configurable, and expose transcript collection without requiring section composition. - Register the transcript contributor in a process-wide default registry that retains no request state. ## Testing - Add unit coverage for role and tool attribution, optional evidence sources, orphaned and named tool outputs, registry reuse, and request-specific entry limits. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: 672818f493e54a702acbeefe9c5f11b57e9263f183f6690f7b8eac35ff3649ee -->

records.content: Support per-tool MCP output limits ## What changed - Add a positive `output_token_limit` setting to each entry under an MCP server's `tools` configuration. - Apply the most restrictive limit when plugin and user policies overlap, while keeping approval policy independent. - Carry the effective MCP output budget in conversation history so tool output, post-tool hook responses, and resumed sessions use the same truncation limit. ## Testing - Cover configuration parsing, serialization, schema validation, and plugin policy merging. - Cover MCP output below and above the configured limit, post-tool hook responses, and session resume. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: 5c822b0953cd06bb89e5560dde27bffe2b3c6f9af73968f7fc151fbc6b3c94f7 -->

records.content: Add app-server notification media filtering ## What changed - Add the disabled-by-default `omit_app_server_notification_media` feature. - When enabled, remove inline image and audio content from `item/started`, `item/completed`, and `rawResponseItem/completed` notifications, including tool output and image-generation results. - Keep the media in model input; the filter only changes app-server notifications. ## Testing - Verify that image content is absent from all three notification types while the model request still receives it. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: bfa112381b1f03dd1d2a87c9fb40a6733b7bb3f5237ef2b0ccd713673feddecd -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Optimize history item lookups
records.content: Optimize history item lookups ## What changed - Lazily index items in larger thread-history turns so late updates can reuse their positions after turn completion and rollback. - Map reverse-history search matches back to Unicode byte ranges with a linear scan. - Preserve first-occurrence semantics for duplicate item IDs and Unicode match boundaries. ## Testing - Cover indexed duplicate updates before and after the indexing threshold. - Cover retained-turn updates after rollback and Unicode history-search ranges. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: 5112b5f9c09abdb5e56243d4450d82d9a02cbd1e5f5f854b6c3086c06f531609 -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Restrict cloud task credentials to trusted origins
records.content: Restrict cloud task credentials to trusted origins ## Why Cloud task requests can use saved ChatGPT credentials, so their destination must be constrained before authentication is loaded or any request is made. ## What changed - Validate `CODEX_CLOUD_TASKS_BASE_URL` against trusted ChatGPT HTTPS origins on port 443 and reject URLs containing user information, queries, or fragments. - Disable redirects for cloud task backend and environment-discovery clients so credentials are never forwarded to a redirect destination. - Normalize the validated base URL before configuring authentication and HTTP clients. ## Testing Add a CLI integration test that verifies a custom cloud backend is rejected without receiving a request, while the staging origin continues to use explicit token authentication. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: 722d0118de9cbb6e26a45ae3579ec891d5be8c3017dda4eeb4224f7b3933ef61 -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Refresh MCP HTTP helper headers after authorization failures
records.content: Refresh MCP HTTP helper headers after authorization failures ## What changed - Re-run the HTTP headers helper after a same-origin `POST` receives a `401` or `403`, and retry the request once when the effective headers changed. - Share refreshes across concurrent rejected requests, retain the previous headers when refresh fails, and keep the retry within the original timeout. - Allow helpers to supply `Authorization` while preserving explicit OAuth or bearer credentials, OAuth insufficient-scope challenges, and redirect safety checks. ## Testing - Cover rotating helper headers for MCP tool calls and same-origin OAuth token refreshes. - Cover concurrent rejections, failed and unchanged refreshes, retry limits, timeouts, and redirects. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: 6413c0175caedd3b579665b44f8a9b2c3d895fe1df99d04e310c1a5f45744ada -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Refresh runtimes for remote plugin state changes
records.content: Refresh runtimes for remote plugin state changes ## Why Enabling, disabling, or reinstalling a cached remote plugin can change its effective MCP servers, hooks, and skills without materializing a new bundle. These transitions need to invalidate plugin consumers just like bundle updates and removals do. ## What changed - Report a unified set of changed remote plugins and their affected capabilities for materializations, removals, and installed-state changes. - Derive enablement and reinstall changes by comparing installed snapshots, while keeping materialization metadata separate for hook trust handling. - Preserve removal notifications even when stale cache cleanup fails, and use all reported changes to refresh loaded plugin state and runtime consumers. ## Testing Added coverage for cached plugin enablement, disablement, removal, and reinstallation, including removal when cache cleanup cannot complete. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: 1c19222b6e4ec640fbe5525d374dddf209a32c7e12356ca58215fbaef804ce25 -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Preserve one-shot exec when unified exec is disabled
records.content: Preserve one-shot exec when unified exec is disabled ## Why Managed configuration can disable resumable unified execution while leaving shell tools enabled. This should not remove command execution entirely or grant access to retained processes. ## What changed - Keep `exec_command` available in completion-only mode when `unified_exec` is disabled. - Remove `tty`, `yield_time_ms`, `session_id`, and `write_stdin` from that mode, and add a `timeout_ms` argument. - Terminate one-shot commands on timeout or turn cancellation, reporting timed-out commands with exit code 124. ## Testing Added integration coverage for tool availability, timeout cleanup, and interruption cleanup under managed configuration. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: c1072993d096a19ffe474d7256a5d6c5c1c95e2d324f0a0bc270242d82c7af37 -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Add shared Guardian context primitives
records.content: Add shared Guardian context primitives ## What changed - Add the `codex-guardian-context` crate for assembling structured context shared by synchronous Guardian review and asynchronous scoring. - Preserve transcript entry roles and original byte counts, and let section contributors declare shared or consumer-specific scope. - Collect applicable sections in registration order, skip optional sections, and fail the collection when required evidence is missing. - Provide UTF-8-safe prefix/suffix truncation with approximate omitted-token accounting. ## Testing - Cover scoped registry collection, ordering, optional sections, required-evidence failures, truncation markers, and UTF-8 boundaries. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: 57f7674e341d2a97fe3658f2f21c491c3a64e9309ec5a38dd5c164e4cd1d1eac -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Give Guardian classifications distinct turn identities
records.content: Give Guardian classifications distinct turn identities ## What changed - Generate a UUIDv7 turn ID for each Guardian classification and preserve it across retries. - Record the owning turn as `parent_turn_id` and propagate its trusted `root_turn_id` when known, including through the tool lifecycle extension API. - Omit ambiguous or unknown root lineage and keep classification identities distinct when reusing Guardian sessions and WebSocket connections. ## Testing - Cover classification metadata across retries, connection reuse, concurrent samples, auth refresh, and consecutive owning turns. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: b93de179de4b8fe5ca181b2702cb0d42491abcc845c2cb745493e012b1af7713 -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Support configurable timeouts for thread shell commands
records.content: Support configurable timeouts for thread shell commands ## What changed - Add an optional `timeoutMs` parameter to `thread/shellCommand` and propagate it to user shell execution. - Preserve the one-hour default when the parameter is omitted or `null`, allow longer deadlines, and treat `0` as an immediate timeout. - Reject negative or otherwise invalid values before execution. Timing out an auxiliary shell command leaves its active turn running. ## Testing - Cover default, extended, immediate, invalid, standalone, active-turn, and interruption behavior. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: 1b0f991574adc74bc069b338bfadaa4bf203f5953a55ba2eb1d122ea783201a4 -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Clarify proactive multi-agent delegation guidance
records.content: Clarify proactive multi-agent delegation guidance ## What changed - Limit the proactive-mode override to earlier developer instructions that require an explicit delegation request. - Preserve user requests as higher-priority guidance. - Encourage root agents and subagents to delegate parallel work when doing so could improve speed or quality. ## Testing - Update the multi-agent world-state snapshot for the revised proactive-mode message. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: e224de8ee301adce313b62733d44acdb3328809292a1ee1a45053f5f99bbe85f -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Preload plugin recommendations during session startup
records.content: Preload plugin recommendations during session startup ## Why Fetching plugin recommendations while building the first-turn context delays that context when the recommendation catalog is not already cached. ## What changed - Start fetching recommendations during session initialization, in parallel with MCP and plugin setup, and reuse the in-flight request when building context. - Centralize the feature checks that enable plugin recommendations. - Prevent an invalidated recommendation request from repopulating the cache after a newer request has completed. ## Testing Added coverage for startup feature gating, reuse of the in-flight fetch, legacy behavior when recommendations are unavailable, and cache invalidation races. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: dd1fe7b070571b38f500f394d8c484ee10db4f8def16d7e9ecc9f852e6e0749b -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Match Windows shell guidance to the executor platform
records.content: Match Windows shell guidance to the executor platform ## What changed - Include Windows safety guidance in the `exec_command` tool description when a single ready environment reports Windows as its executor platform. - Omit that guidance when the selected executor reports a non-Windows platform. - Preserve the host-based behavior when platform information is unavailable or the tool can target multiple environments. ## Testing - Cover Windows, non-Windows, unknown-platform, and multi-environment tool plans. - Verify remote environments expose guidance that matches their target OS. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: 6bd15659bd5451e6251a7a848009019b5001b9cc8769ba9450802c26c108fe7f -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Restrict async user messages to questions

Ask models to keep these questions concise, understandable, and at an appropriate level of abstraction for the user and task. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: 1a5109a8654368f2a50cce348fe0113c11449d2c426fde6d954c6f4d4fd4f415 -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Test resuming compressed shared rollouts
records.content: Test resuming compressed shared rollouts ## What changed Add an end-to-end core test that compresses a parent and forked child rollout, then resumes the child through paginated history loading. Verify that the resumed model input: - retains the persisted compaction checkpoint and inherited history; - includes child history through the fork boundary; - excludes obsolete pre-checkpoint and post-fork parent messages; and - reads the compressed ancestor without materializing its JSONL file. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: b0d479759fbc28f2aad4d5fa8fcdd5e919e773056c49f563639745b2e958fab5 -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Measure Codex home usage at app-server startup
records.content: Measure Codex home usage at app-server startup ## What changed - Scan regular files under `CODEX_HOME` in a background blocking task when standalone app-server metrics are enabled. - Record `codex.app_server.codex_home.size_bytes` for the entire home and the `sessions` and `archived_sessions` subdirectories. - Avoid following symlinks, discard incomplete scans, and cancel scanning during shutdown. <!-- copyberry-projection-id: 94333a024b4259888f930ee3920a27491b910d528ae7721874fb38e48177489c -->

records.title: OpenAI Codex: Support compression for shared rollout lineages
records.content: Support compression for shared rollout lineages ## Why Rollout compression skips files that participate in paginated fork lineages because lineage readers rely on byte offsets into the original JSONL. This prevents shared rollout history from being compressed. ## What changed - Add a seekable rollout reader that preserves logical JSONL offsets for plain and zstd-compressed files without materializing compressed data beside the rollout. - Use the reader for lineage validation, model-context replay, and SQLite history projection, including when compression races with a read. - Add the opt-in `local_thread_store_shared_compression` feature. records.title: OpenClaw: Prepare compiled subprocesses for finite source test runs
records.content: ### Summary Compile declared application subprocess roots once per finite repository test invocation, while preserving separate-process isolation and live-source watch behavior. ### Problem to solve Vitest transforms TypeScript in its own process, but a separately launched Node child cannot reuse those transformations. Source-mode tests therefore repeatedly start a TypeScript loader for application workers, and short readiness deadlines can include that loading work rather than just the behavior under test. Installed OpenClaw already runs compiled JavaScript. The missing piece is a fresh, owned subprocess build for source tests—not a different SQLite locking or migration policy. ### Proposed solution Use the repository's existing compiler and test runner to lazily prepare one fresh generation of declared application workers and the private TUI runtime graph. Share it across the invocation's projects/shards, verify source/output/native-asset fingerprints, and retain it until all borrowers and child processes have joined. Never adopt checkout `dist` or another invocation's output. Keep standalone Vitest and watch runs on live source. Preserve Node/Bun argument handling, platform supervision, read-only snapshot boundaries and uncertainty retention. No new configuration option or dependency is needed. ### Alternatives considered Reusing arbitrary checkout build output risks testing stale code. Replacing subprocesses with worker threads does not preserve the SQLite same-inode file-lock boundary. Increasing deadlines or clearing transform caches would hide startup costs instead of assigning compilation and cleanup to an owner. ### Impact Developers get subprocess tests whose readiness budgets measure the child behavior after preparation, with explicit build failures and lifecycle checks. records.content: [memory] openai-compatible embeddings need configurable throttle + honor Retry-After + enable Batch API ## Problem When using an `openai-compatible` provider (千帆 bge-large-zh, 阿里百炼, 火山方舟, etc.) for `memory.search`, OpenClaw fires embedding requests in a tight loop with no throttle, no concurrency limit, and no `Retry-After` honoring. The provider returns 429 (TPM rate limit), the indexer retries immediately, and the daily quota burns out within seconds — leaving the index dirty and `vector search` permanently disabled. Real log: ``` openai-compatible embeddings failed: HTTP 429: {"error":{"code":"tpm_rate_limit_exceeded", "message":"Rate limit reached for TPM", "type":"rate_limit_exceeded"}, "id":"as-1k2xjjsf5e"} ``` ## Environment - OpenClaw: v2026.9.1-beta.1 (1d96e5a) - `memory.search.provider`: `openai-compatible` - `memory.search.remote.baseUrl`: `https://qianfan.baidubce.com/v2/` - `memory.search.model`: `bge-large-zh` - `memory.search.sources`: `["memory", "sessions"]` (~500 files reindexed) - `memory.search.remote.batch.enabled`: `true` (silently ignored, see below) ## Repro 1. Configure `memory.search.provider = "openai-compatible"` against a TPM-limited endpoint 2. Trigger any full reindex — e.g. by changing `model`, changing `sources`, or upgrading the binary 3. Observe 429 storm during reindex; `Indexing session files…` stalls at e.g. `552/556` 4. `vector search` stays `paused`; memory.search effectively broken until config rolled back ## Root Cause (verified in source) ### 1. records.title: OpenClaw: fix(build): ignore tool scratch churn in boundary topology walks
records.content: ## What Problem This Solves `pnpm check:changed` intermittently fails during extension-lint preparation with: ``` Error: Boundary configuration or resolution topology changed during compilation prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts failed with exit code 1 ``` `BoundaryInputSnapshot.namespace()` (new in #132532, refined in #132603) records every file name under installed roots with no scratch exclusions. Vite writes a transient `node_modules/.vite-temp/<config>.timestamp-<ms>-<rand>.mjs` bundle on every ESM config load and async-unlinks it (installed vite 8.2.2, `loadConfigFromBundledFile`), and jiti keeps hash-named `.mjs` files under `node_modules/.cache`. Any sibling task loading a vitest/vite config in the same checkout mints such names between the before-compile and after-compile topology walks, the digests differ, and `record()` throws — discarding an already-successful native emit. Stale leftover scratch files also spuriously invalidated warm boundary caches via the signature. ## Why This Change Was Made Fix at the scanner's owner, not by retrying: skip dot-entries under installed roots except `.pnpm`. npm package names cannot start with `.`, so bare-specifier resolution never enters these directories; pnpm's virtual store is the one dot-entry lookups traverse (symlink targets) and stays in the walk. Install-driven changes to skipped metadata (`.modules.yaml`, `.bin`) remain covered by the lockfile and `.modules.yaml` content hashes already in the signature. This kills the whole churn class (vite, jiti, vitest caches, future tools) instead of denylisting one directory name, and stops the walk from pointlessly traversing ~11k vitest-cache entries per scan. Named tradeoff: vite's EACCES/deno fallback writes `<config>.timestamp-*.mjs` next to the config file outside installed roots and is not excluded — an unwritable `node_modules` breaks pnpm itself long before this scanner. ## User Impact Developers and CI running `pnpm check:changed` (or `pnpm lint`) wh

records.title: OpenClaw: fix(line): apply a group's configured skill scope
records.content: Closes #132496 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where an operator who narrows the skills available in one LINE group gets no narrowing at all. `channels.line.groups.<groupId>.skills` passes config validation and is listed in the LINE channel docs, so the setting looks accepted — and then the agent answers that group with the full default skill set. Nothing reports that the setting was dropped. ## Why This Change Was Made The behavior contract: a group's configured skill scope applies to the turns that answer that group, and an empty list means no skills, exactly as it does on every other channel. The group entry is already read on this path — LINE resolves `systemPrompt` from it into `GroupSystemPrompt` — so this is one field of an entry the code already loads. The change resolves that entry once instead of twice, reads `skills` alongside `systemPrompt`, carries it on the inbound context, and passes it to the turn as `skillFilter`. That is the same wiring Telegram (`group-config-helpers.ts:73`), Slack (`monitor/message-handler/dispatch.ts:420`) and Matrix (`matrix/monitor/handler.ts:565`) already use; LINE was the outlier. Two decisions worth stating: - **An empty list stays a scope.** `skills: []` means "no skills", so presence decides whether a filter is passed, never length. Dropping empty arrays would silently turn the strictest setting into the loosest. - **The scope is group-only.** LINE's schema exposes `skills` on group entries only, so direct chats carry no filter, and a direct chat is left exactly as before. Non-goal: LINE deliberately omits `tools`/`toolsBySender` from its group schema (`buildGroupEntrySchema().omit(...)`), so tool policy still cannot be set per LINE group. This change does not add it. Production delta is +24/−11. The growth is one resolved value threaded from the config entry to the turn; the offsetting removals come from resolving the group entry once instead of inline inside the `extra` block. ## User Impact `channels.line.gr

records.title: OpenClaw: fix(heartbeat): admit restart-sentinel in isTargetedUnscheduledWake
records.content: Fixes #131850 Fixes #131490 ## What Problem This Solves ### Heartbeat restart-sentinel fix `isTargetedUnscheduledWake()` does not admit the source `restart-sentinel`, so when the target agent has no recurring heartbeat schedule, the restart-sentinel's immediate wake is dropped and the queued restart event never triggers an agent turn. Restart continuation silently depends on heartbeat being enabled. ### Cron timeout classification fix Isolated agent setup timeouts were being misclassified as permanent failures (triggering immediate retry exhaustion) when they should be treated as transient (eligible for cron retry). ### CLI update --dry-run fix The `openclaw update status` subcommand was accepting `--dry-run` even though it's not supported at the subcommand level. records.title: OpenClaw: fix(xai): canonicalize OAuth model during setup verification
records.content: ## Summary Fix xAI OAuth pairing in Model Setup when the stable `xai/auto` selector is verified before its authenticated live catalog metadata has reached the isolated setup runtime. The observed failure was a literal `auto` request sent to `https://api.x.ai/v1/responses`, returning 404 and surfacing as: > The selected model was not found by the provider. This is adjacent to #122872, but the affected composition is the transactional provider-auth setup flow: a fresh staged OAuth credential plus the read-only inference verification runtime. ## Root cause xAI device login durably selects `xai/auto`, which is correct. Its concrete target and OAuth proxy transport come from authenticated live discovery. During setup, the newly staged credential was not represented in the catalog used by the isolated verification run, so the route retained the static API origin and forwarded `auto` literally. Thinking level is not causal: setup verification intentionally uses thinking/reasoning `off`. ## Fix - Discover the authenticated xAI OAuth catalog during device login. - Add a generic `inferenceProbeConfigPatch` to provider auth results. - Apply that patch only to setup execution/verification config. - Keep durable `xai/auto` dynamic; do not persist its point-in-time canonical model. - Use the xAI OAuth CLI proxy for the probe. - When changing OAuth origins, discard stale xAI per-model overrides and strip provider API keys, auth flags, headers, and request auth/header fields. - Retain non-authenticated request policy. - Leave xAI API-key onboarding unchanged. ## Security and transaction boundaries - OAuth tokens remain in the staged auth-profile store and are not serialized into model config or logs. - The authenticated canonical mapping is ephemeral. - Failed catalog or inference verification occurs before durable credential/config persistence. - Existing credential-bearing transport overrides cannot cross into the OAuth proxy route. ## Tests - xAI extension suite: 483/483 passed.

records.title: OpenClaw: fix(worktrees): reclaim archived checkouts and bound disk allocation
records.content: Closes #132670 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where operators archiving worktree sessions would retain the full checkout indefinitely, while new tasks could continue allocating checkouts without a count limit or useful disk-space admission check. Repeated tasks could exhaust the volume needed by the Gateway and SQLite. ## Why This Change Was Made The managed-worktree service now owns a default limit of 30 live checkouts and a shared allocation lease across creation, restoration, and snapshot removal. Admission budgets checkout and provisioned-file writes, repository setup, and a 4–16 GiB operational reserve on each participating filesystem. Snapshot cleanup uses a smaller reserve so operators can recover space safely. Existing valid checkouts remain reusable at the limit; active or manual work is never evicted during allocation. Session archive now uses the existing fenced lifecycle to snapshot and remove the exact bound checkout. Explicit unarchive and authorized human inbound messages restore the original commit and saved files before admitting work. Automatic archive performs cleanup after its SQLite writer is released, and normal GC retries archived or missing owners while preserving active admissions, worker placements, locks, and uncertain ownership. Broken Git administrative links refuse reuse with recovery guidance rather than silently adopting an unusable checkout. ## User Impact Archiving a worktree conversation releases its checkout without deleting conversation history. Dirty files, non-ignored untracked files, provisioned files, and unpushed commits retain the existing snapshot/restore contract. Snapshots still expire after 30 days; missing snapshots or source repositories produce an explicit recovery error rather than a fresh empty checkout. Installations already above 30 retain protected work and must archive/remove an unused checkout before creating another. There are no new configuration keys, environment variables, dependencies, or data

It also aligns mixed-action schemas with executable behavior so rejected fields are not advertised as valid updates. records.content: Fixes #132625 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where users running a one-shot inference against a reasoning model that cannot disable thinking (e.g. Z.AI GLM-5.x with `thinkingLevelMap: { off: "low" }`) would get a provider 400 rejection when they did not pass `--thinking`: `openclaw infer model run --model zai/glm-5.3-flash --prompt "hi"` emitted a thinking-disabled payload (`This model always engages in thinking and cannot be disabled`). This mirrors how the openrouter and generic reasoning-effort branches in the same function already treat a mapped `off` level, and matches the agent path, which maps `off` through `thinkingLevelMap` before building requests. Explicit `--thinking off` behavior is unchanged (it already resolves through the map); models without an `off` mapping keep the existing disabled payload. Note: #132671 fixes the same symptom at the CLI default-resolution layer (resolving the provider's thinking default when `--thinking` is absent). This PR instead fixes the payload emission site, which also covers custom providers that carry `thinkingLevelMap` without a plugin profile, and does not change default thinking behavior for unrelated providers. ## User Impact Operators using Z.AI GLM-5.x (or any OpenAI-compatible model whose config maps thinking `off` to a concrete level) can run one-shot `infer model run` calls without `--thinking` and get a successful response instead of a provider 400. records.content: Follow-up to #132690, which fixed the first of two gh-shape defects on the same merge path. ## What Problem This Solves Agent merges to `main` still abort, now one step later: ``` merge-verify passed for PR #132638 Merge outcome: authoritative PR/main metadata unavailable or invalid ``` `merge_outcome_read_remote` compares the GraphQL repository object against the identity captured earlier from `gh repo view --json id,nameWithOwner,url`: ``` select({id,url,nameWithOwner} == $repo and (.ref.target.oid | oid)) ``` Those two sources report different ids for the same repository: ``` gh repo view : {"id":1103012935, "nameWithOwner":"openclaw/openclaw", ...} GraphQL : {"id":"R_kgDOQb6kRw","databaseId":1103012935, ...} ``` gh gives the REST database id; GraphQL gives the node id. The object equality can never hold, so `jq -e` fails and admission stops. #132690 let admission past the first check; this is the next one on the same path. ## Why This Change Was Made Select `databaseId` alongside `id` and accept whichever representation gh supplied. `url` and `nameWithOwner` still have to match exactly, so the repository remains pinned - only the id comparison learns that one repository has two legitimate id shapes. Verified against live data: the corrected predicate passes the complete observation validation for #132638 and returns the expected `{main, pr}` object. ## User Impact Restores `scripts/pr merge-run` for maintainers and agents. Without it the documented landing flow gets as far as merge-verify and then stops without merging. ## Evidence **Why no test caught either defect.** The fixture spread a single identity object into both the `gh repo view` response and the GraphQL response, so the two could never disagree. records.title: OpenClaw: perf(tasks): bound tasks.list page selection
records.content: Fixes #101716 ## What Problem This Solves The task registry page path still filters and fully sorts every matching task before slicing the requested `tasks.list` page. On long-lived gateways with large task histories, that keeps the hot Control UI polling path at O(n log n) sorting cost and requires an O(n) candidate array. ## What Changed - keep only the prefix needed to answer the requested `offset + limit` page; - deterministically prune the candidate buffer whenever it reaches two page windows; - preserve the existing newest-first ordering and task-id tie-break; - preserve status, agent, session, access-filter, cloning, cursor, and `hasMore` semantics; - add a structural regression proving activity sorts stay bounded to two requested page windows rather than the full matching registry. For the common first-page path, sorting becomes O(n log page-size) with O(page-size) temporary candidates. Deeper offset cursors intentionally increase the retained window because the existing offset contract must remain exact. ## Scope Two files changed. Production: +38/-19 lines (net +19). Test: +52 lines. No protocol, config, persistence, task-state, or Control UI response-shape changes. ## Validation The branch is one commit on current upstream `main`. The regression is source-structural rather than timing-based: with 20 matching tasks and `offset=4`, `limit=3`, the old implementation sorts all 20 records; the repaired path keeps every sort at or below two seven-record page windows. No fork CI runs are attached to the branch yet. Upstream CI should run the focused task-registry and gateway task suites after the PR is opened. AI-assisted contribution. I reviewed the current registry owner, the prior partial optimization history, pagination semantics, and the final production/test diff.

records.title: OpenClaw: fix(codex): preserve structured image timeouts
records.content: Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/83416 ## What Problem This Solves The retained Codex `view_image` fallback used the same configured timeout for two different owners: the outer app-server RPC watchdog and each inner provider request. At the boundary, the outer watchdog could win first and replace the image owner's structured provider result with a generic `OpenClaw dynamic tool call timed out` failure. The inner owner also excluded media preparation and gave provider setup, each request, a reasoning-only retry, each sequential image, and every model fallback a fresh full timeout. Increasing only the outer timer could therefore still mask a late stage, while multiplying configured timeouts would make the total operation unbounded. ## Solution - Start one absolute image-inspection deadline before compression and media preparation. - Derive that deadline from the longest selected image request timeout and cap the whole operation at 600 seconds. - Carry one abort signal through reference access, media runtime initialization, image loading/optimization, provider setup, requests, retries, sequential images, and model fallbacks. - Give every provider stage and fallback request only its remaining operation time. - Keep Codex's outer `item/tool/call` watchdog at 630 seconds so the owner can return its structured timeout result. - Remove duplicate provider-timeout discovery from the Codex adapter; the image owner remains the canonical timeout policy owner. This does not add config, protocol, dependency, or compatibility surfaces. ## Evidence ### Parent-red on current main before the production edit The focused regression on the exact parent reproduced the race: ```text owner request budget: 1000ms outer watchdog budget: 1000ms result: generic outer dynamic-tool timeout ``` Additional parent-red receipts exposed the complete owner gap: ```text generic runtime setup consumed 400ms: request received 1000ms, expected 600ms reasoning-only request consumed 400ms: r

records.title: OpenClaw: fix(maintainers): recover stalled merge attempts without losing evidence
records.content: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where maintainers could not finish an explicitly reviewed merge recovery after a rejected or interrupted request left a retained intent. Ordinary `merge-run` correctly refuses to infer non-execution from an OPEN PR, but the native workflow offered no way to record a separate operator decision. This stranded the otherwise green refusal-marker repair in #132556. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds `scripts/pr merge-recover <PR> <OUTCOME_OID> --confirmed-operator-recovery` to the existing merge owner. It requires the exact retained, unaccepted immediate intent; the same prepared head, method, and PR identity; fresh review/required-check/admission validation; and a currently immediate route without auto, queue, or admin bypass. The old outcome becomes a parent of the new intent, which records the authenticated actor and explicit recovery decision. The exact-OID update consumes that decision, so reusing it cannot dispatch again. This never declares the old request rejected or unexecuted. Ordinary reconciliation remains read-only with respect to merge dispatch, and an error message or OPEN observation never authorizes recovery. Each new dispatch uses an exclusive attempt-qualified capture; earlier logs remain unchanged during recovery, and the shared cleanup owner recognizes both legacy and new captures. Normal successful worktree cleanup still applies; retained Git outcome history survives it. ## User Impact Maintainer tooling only; no application runtime, configuration, dependency, schema, or provider-policy changes. records.title: OpenClaw: fix(codex): reap orphaned app-server children after a hard-killed gateway
records.content: Related: #132413 (follow-up 3) ## What Problem This Solves Resolves a problem where a hard-killed (SIGKILLed) gateway orphans the detached Codex app-server child process. The stdio transport spawns the child as a detached process-group leader, so graceful shutdown can group-kill it — but nothing reaped survivors on the next boot. The orphan keeps executing the in-flight native turn against the pre-restart rollout state, and a fast gateway restart spawns a fresh app-server that shares the same CODEX_HOME with the still-draining orphan. This was named as follow-up 3 in #132413. ## Why This Change Was Made Per the gateway audit doctrine (record facts where they happen), every stdio app-server spawn now registers the child's exact identity (pid + `ps lstart`) plus the owning process identity in the codex plugin's SQLite keyed-state store (namespace `app-server-processes`; no schema change, no pidfiles), and removes the row on child exit. A memoized, bounded (~5s) reaper runs at gateway startup as a plugin service and is also awaited before the first app-server spawn — plugin services start post-attach, so a turn can beat the service. Evidence rules are fail-closed: a single full `ps -axo` snapshot (which exits 0 regardless of target presence) proves owner death and child presence/identity; a final per-pid check immediately gates each SIGKILL with no await in between; `ps -p` exits nonzero for missing pids and therefore cannot distinguish absent from failed, so per-pid reads are used only where both outcomes take the same no-kill action. Group kill is applied only to confirmed group leaders (QA-mode children share their owner's group and get a direct pid signal). Row removal uses compare-and-delete so a judgment made against a stale snapshot can never clobber a row re-registered by a live owner. records.title: OpenClaw: fix(line): let a quote of the bot address it in a group
records.content: Fixes #132036 ## What Problem This Solves Quoting the bot in a LINE group did nothing. No reply, no log line, no sign the message had been gated — and quoting is the gesture LINE's own UI pushes for answering someone in a busy group. LINE groups require a mention by default (`bot-handlers.ts` reads `groupConfig?.requireMention !== false`), and the plugin had no way to notice that a message was aimed at it. Core has had the concept the whole time: `src/channels/mention-gating.ts` defines `reply_to_bot`, `quoted_bot` and `bot_thread_participant`, and `docs/channels/groups.md` publishes which channels produce each one. LINE appeared in none of the three rows, and the code matched — it passed a hardcoded `implicitMentionKinds: []` while Discord, Mattermost, Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp and Zalo all supply facts. ## Why This Change Was Made The fact was missing, not the machinery, so this adds the fact and nothing else. LINE now emits `quoted_bot` through the same `implicitMentionKindWhen` helper every other producer uses; the decision, the config gating and the precedence all stay in core. The one piece LINE cannot borrow is how to know the quoted message is ours. WhatsApp compares the quoted message's sender identity and Telegram and Discord read the author id straight off the update, because their platforms include it. LINE's webhook carries `quotedMessageId` and nothing else — no author, no snippet — so recognising our own message means remembering what we sent. `outbound-message-log.ts` is that memory: one bounded map from message id to account id, written at `recordLineOutboundActivity`, which is the single funnel every LINE send already passes through, so no new call sites appear. It is keyed by account rather than conversation because a LINE message id is unique and can only be quoted from the conversation it was sent to, which makes the account match the whole check. Kept LINE-local rather than promoted to a core seam on purpose. Every other channel gets the author

records.title: OpenClaw: fix(maintainers): accept the repository id shape gh returns during merge admission
records.content: ## What Problem This Solves Every agent-driven merge to `main` aborts. `scripts/pr merge-run <PR>` fails closed with: ``` Merge outcome: invalid repository identity No merge retry. Repeated merge-run only reconciles a recorded attempt. ``` Merge admission validates the repository identity returned by `gh repo view --json id,nameWithOwner,url` and required `.id` to be a non-empty **string**. Current `gh` reports a repository's REST database id as a JSON **number**: ``` {"id":1103012935,"nameWithOwner":"openclaw/openclaw","url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw"} ``` The `select` yields nothing, `jq -e` exits 4, and admission stops before doing any work. Reproduced on `gh` 2.98.0 with the real binary (`gh_plain` deliberately bypasses shims, and no `~/bin/gh` shim exists on the host). Note the asymmetry that made this easy to miss: `gh pr view --json id` returns a GraphQL node string (`PR_kwDO...`), so `prId` was always fine. Only the repository id is numeric. ## Why This Change Was Made Accept either scalar for `.id`. The identity check's job is to confirm gh returned a well-formed repository identity, and a database id is well-formed - it simply is not a string. The parts that decide *which* repository this is are unchanged: `nameWithOwner` must still match `owner/name`, and `url` must still be an https URL ending in `/` + `nameWithOwner`. So a missing, empty, or non-scalar id, and a url that does not belong to the named repository, are all still rejected. This narrows nothing about the duplicate-merge protection added in #132173; it only stops that protection from failing closed on every merge. ## User Impact Maintainers and agents can land PRs through the documented `scripts/pr` flow again. The native merge path ignored the prepared gate mode and entered a watcher that can only observe pull-request runs. ## Why This Change Was Made Merge reloads the prepared mode and revalidates hosted evidence through the existing canonical prepare verifier before continuing to required-check verification. records.title: OpenClaw: fix(wizard): offer the plugins that are actually active
records.content: Closes #127578 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where the CLI plugin wizard, during onboarding and `configure`, offers plugins that are switched off and skips plugins that are actually running. Both directions are user visible. A plugin explicitly disabled in config is still offered, so the wizard solicits settings for it and then warns that config is present while the plugin is disabled. A plugin activated through slot selection, auto-enable, workspace policy or a platform default is left out, so the wizard never asks about something that does run. ## Why This Change Was Made The inventory decided activation itself: ```ts return plugin.enabledByDefault || entry?.enabled === true; ``` An explicit `enabled: false` is not `=== true`, so that arm falls through to the manifest default and the plugin stays in the list. It is loaded through `createLazyRuntimeModule` alongside the existing metadata snapshot import, so the wizard still does not pull the plugin graph in eagerly. ## User Impact The wizard offers the plugins that are actually active. records.title: OpenClaw: fix(line): deliver a code block the Flex card cannot hold
records.content: ## What Problem This Solves When an agent answers on LINE with a fenced code block longer than 2000 characters — a config file, a log excerpt, a diff — the reply keeps the first 2000 characters and throws the rest away. The card ends mid-token with an ellipsis, and the sentence after it is delivered as written, so the reply reads as complete when it is not: ![LINE code card cut at `const line52`, then a bare `const` and an ellipsis, followed by the message "That is the whole file."](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2bb468ab-051f-45be-a2dd-5cfca837c47d) That screenshot is a 120-line file. 67 of those lines are not in the conversation anywhere. Nothing about LINE requires the cut. `POST /v2/bot/message/validate/push` accepts a Flex text of 2 000, 5 000, and 10 000 characters alike — the 2000 is this plugin's own display budget for the code card: ``` len=2000 {} HTTP_STATUS=200 len=2001 {} HTTP_STATUS=200 len=5000 {} HTTP_STATUS=200 len=10000 {} HTTP_STATUS=200 ``` Every other block in the same reply already survives. Prose is chunked at LINE's 5000-character limit and sent across several messages. A table too large for its card degrades to text through `formatOversizedTableAsBullets` and keeps every row. A code block is the only block that loses content. ## Why This Change Was Made `processLineMessage` already owns the "this block does not fit its card" decision — the table loop right above the code loop makes exactly that call and falls back to text. The code loop had no such branch, so `convertCodeBlockToFlexBubble`'s internal truncation was the only thing standing between a long block and the wire. records.title: NanoBot: Session message rate-limit state retains expired one-shot sessions
records.content: ### Bug Description `SendSessionMessageTool` keeps one timestamp deque per source session in `_sent_at`. Expired timestamps are removed only when that same source sends again: ```python sent_at = self._sent_at.setdefault(source.session_key, deque()) while sent_at and sent_at[0] <= cutoff: sent_at.popleft() ``` The tool instance is registered once for the lifetime of `AgentLoop`, so source sessions that send one message and never return leave their key and expired deque resident for the rest of the gateway process. Long-running API/WebUI deployments with many temporary sessions therefore accumulate rate-limit state that no longer protects any active window. ### Steps to Reproduce On current `main` (`caab883f`): 1. Create a `SendSessionMessageTool` with an injected monotonic clock. 2. Send one message from each of 1,000 distinct source session keys at `t=0`. 3. Advance the clock to `t=3600`. 4. Send one message from a new source session. Observed state: ```text after_initial_sends: keys=1000 timestamps=1000 after_one_hour_and_new_send: keys=1001 live_timestamps=1 expired_keys=1000 ``` The later send cleans only its own source deque; none of the 1,000 expired entries is reclaimed. ### Expected Behavior Rate-limit state should be bounded by source sessions with timestamps in the active rolling window. Expired one-shot source entries should be reclaimed without requiring those sources to send again, while preserving the existing per-source rolling-minute semantics. An opportunistic sweep under the existing send lock, amortized to run at most once per rate-limit window, would avoid per-session timers and avoid scanning the registry on every send. ### Relevant Logs ```shell No runtime error is emitted; the stale state is visible in the tool's rate-limit registry. ``` ### nanobot Version Current `main` at `caab883f` ### Python Version 3.12 ### Operating System macOS ### Channel / Platform WebSocket / long-running gateway ### LLM Provider Provider-independent ### Additional

records.title: NanoBot: Let a runtime-context block opt out of history persistence (`ephemeral` blocks)
records.content: ### Problem / Motivation Runtime-context blocks currently have exactly one lifecycle: appended to the user message, persisted into that session row (`agent/loop.py:725-731` via `append_runtime_context`), and replayed on every later turn (`get_history(include_runtime_context=True)` is the default - `session/manager.py:370-375`). That is the right behavior for the in-tree producer - a WebUI quote is a per-turn fact that belongs in history. But it is the **only** lifecycle the seam offers. A channel or runtime-context provider that needs to state *session-constant* information - a delivery contract like "replies here are spoken aloud; keep to short plain prose" - can only restate it on every message, and each copy is then persisted and replayed forever. We measured this while building an external voice channel: a ~250-token contract became ~7,400 duplicated tokens of history by turn 30, paid again in every turn's prefill and competing with real dialogue under the replay tail-slice - on small context windows the duplicates evict the conversation itself. Core already recognizes this failure class on the assistant side: `_sanitize_assistant_replay_text` exists precisely because replay artifacts "become demonstrations for the model to repeat" (`session/manager.py:195-208`). User-side riders have no equivalent. In-tree channels avoid the problem statically, via the identity template's format-hint ladder - a seam third-party channels cannot extend. ### Proposed Solution An opt-out flag on the block: ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class RuntimeContextBlock: source: str content: str ephemeral: bool = False # new ``` Ephemeral blocks are appended at request-build time to the **current** message only and never persisted - no `RUNTIME_CONTEXT_HISTORY_META` marker, nothing in the session row, nothing to strip at display time. The default is unchanged, so every existing producer keeps today's behavior. Sizing: `runtime_context.py` plus two call sites in `agent/loop.py`; display/

records.title: NanoBot: Deliver provider retry-wait notices to channels (`RetryWaitEvent` is CLI-only today)
records.content: ### Problem / Motivation When a provider request fails and backs off, core produces a proper event - "Model request failed, retrying in {n}s (attempt {k})" (`providers/base.py:1554-1572`, published as `RetryWaitEvent` by `agent/turn_delivery.py:161-175`). But `ChannelManager` discards every one of them before dispatch: ```python # nanobot/channels/manager.py:740-741 if isinstance(event, RetryWaitEvent): continue ``` The discard is unconditional - it sits outside the `sendProgress` gate, so no configuration can turn it on. The only renderer is the interactive CLI (`cli/terminal.py:371-374`). During a 60–120 s provider backoff, every real channel therefore shows a silently hung turn. Users re-send their message (queuing duplicate work), and channel implementations that want to distinguish "provider is backing off" from "turn is wedged" are pushed into guessing with their own deadman timers. ### Proposed Solution Deliver it through the existing egress path the way progress events already flow, behind the existing per-channel `sendProgress` gate - or, if a rendered chat message feels too intrusive as a default, add `BaseChannel.send_retry_wait(...)` as a default no-op hook so only channels that implement it receive the notice (mirroring `send_delta` / `send_reasoning*`, which already follow that pattern). Either shape is a small diff: the event, its content string, and the dispatch loop all exist; only the discard changes. ### Alternatives Considered - **Channels inferring stalls from their own timers:** what external channels do today - a provider backoff and a genuinely wedged turn are indistinguishable, so the timers misfire in both directions. - **Logging only:** the operator can already see it; the person waiting on the reply cannot. ### Related Component Channel (WeChat, Feishu, Telegram, etc.) ### Additional Context _No response_

records.title: NanoBot: Bound how far back `reasoning_content` / `thinking_blocks` are replayed to the provider
records.content: ### Problem / Motivation `Session.get_history` copies `reasoning_content` and `thinking_blocks` into the replayed history for **every** message, indefinitely: ```python # nanobot/session/manager.py:420-423 entry: dict[str, Any] = {"role": message["role"], "content": content} for key in ("tool_calls", "tool_call_id", "name", "reasoning_content", "thinking_blocks"): if key in message: entry[key] = message[key] ``` Reasoning-only assistant rows are deliberately kept alive (`manager.py:417-419`), and the provider adapters then re-emit every persisted thinking block on the wire (`providers/anthropic_provider.py:306-315`, `providers/bedrock_provider.py:229`). Past-turn reasoning is token-heavy, and provider guidance is generally that it can be dropped once a turn completes - it is needed on the wire only within the current tool loop. Today the only bound is the overall replay token budget, which trims oldest messages wholesale: old reasoning that contributes nothing competes on equal terms with the conversation itself. On small context windows (local models) that evicts genuine dialogue turns earlier than necessary, and every deployment pays prefill for it on every turn. ### Proposed Solution Strip reasoning fields from older rows **at replay time only** - the persisted record stays complete for display, consolidation, and turn recovery (`session/recovery.py:178` reads the persisted field and is unaffected). Replay them only for the most recent assistant turn, using the last user row as the boundary so an unfinished tool loop keeps its thinking blocks intact (providers that require thinking blocks across a tool loop keep working). Make it configurable, e.g.: ``` agents.defaults.replayReasoning: recent | all | none # recent = proposed default ``` `all` preserves today's behavior exactly for anyone who depends on it. ### Alternatives Considered _No response_ ### Related Component Agent / Prompts ### Additional Context _No response_

records.title: NanoBot: Append the "try a different approach" hint to raised tool exceptions too
records.content: ### Problem / Motivation `AgentRunner._run_tool` appends the recovery nudge ```python # nanobot/agent/runner.py:1482 hint = "\n\n[Analyze the error above and try a different approach.]" ``` to error-shaped tool **results** (`runner.py:1550-1566`, under `is_tool_error_result`), to blocked repeated external lookups (`:1483-1494`), and to workspace prep errors (`:1506-1521`) - but a tool that **raises** returns the bare payload: ```python # nanobot/agent/runner.py:1523-1548 (excerpt) except Exception as exc: ... payload = f"Error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}" handled = self._classify_violation( raw_text=str(exc), # Preserve legacy exception payloads without the retry hint. soft_payload=payload, ... ) ``` Raising is how most real failures arrive - network errors, timeouts, permission denials, MCP transport faults - so the strongest retry nudge core has is absent exactly where recovery matters most. Small local models in particular tend to answer a bare `Error: …` by narrating the failure and finalizing instead of trying something else. It is also internally inconsistent: when the call goes through `ToolRegistry.execute` (the `tool is None` path), the registry wraps a raised exception **with** the hint (`agent/tools/registry.py:187-201`) - so the same exception class gets the hint on one execution path and not the other. ### Proposed Solution Append the same hint to the raised-exception payload in `_run_tool` (behind a flag if the legacy payload shape must stay parseable for some caller). This follows the direction 8332c604 already set - "let subagents recover from tool errors": if tool errors now always flow back to the model so it can retry, they should arrive in the shape that best triggers a retry. Small optional cleanup in the same area: a registry-wrapped error re-entering the error-shaped-result branch currently collects the hint twice. ### Alternatives Considered _No response_ ### Related Component Agent / Prompts ### Additional Context _No response_

Cache keys are isolated by credential location, hashed account identity, provider endpoint, and proxy. Login and logout invalidate the provider cache; a generation fence discards any older refresh that finishes after that invalidation without retrying it under the previous identity key. The shared catalog module owns only that cache lifecycle and its small snapshot interface. Authentication, HTTP requests, and payload parsing remain in the existing Codex, Grok, and Copilot provider modules, while built-in fallback metadata remains in the provider registry. Remote catalogs remain authoritative. Curated data only enriches known entries and provides a final fallback, so transient auth, rate-limit, or network failures never empty the model selector. Provider adapters preserve each upstream contract: - OpenAI Codex queries the authenticated Codex models endpoint with a compatibility-gated client version, filters hidden entries, preserves priority order, and imports context-window and reasoning-effort metadata. - xAI Grok reads subscription models and shares hosted X Search capability metadata with the runtime. Hosted search uses xAI's documented balanced five-turn budget. records.title: NanoBot: fix(webui): preserve named pane groups
records.content: ## Problem A pane group can have a user-defined title while still being stored as an implicit group. When removing or deleting panes leaves that group with a single pane, reconciliation treats it like an unnamed implicit group, dissolves it, and loses the custom title. Deleting the active pane also selected the next session from the global topic order, which could move the user to an unrelated conversation even when another pane remained in the same group. ## Changes - Treat persisted pane groups with a custom title as explicit groups during normalization. - Mark a group as explicit whenever it is renamed, including when the normalized title is unchanged. - When deleting the active pane, prefer a surviving pane from the same group before falling back to the surrounding topic order. - Preserve the existing behavior for genuinely unnamed implicit groups. ## Compatibility Previously saved named groups are upgraded in memory through the existing normalization path and are persisted in the canonical explicit form on the next state update. No API or storage-schema migration is required, and older clients already understand the existing `explicit` field. ## User-visible behavior - A custom group title survives after the group is reduced to one pane. - Deleting the active pane keeps the user in the same group when possible. - Refreshing the WebUI preserves the group title and active pane. - Unnamed temporary groups continue to collapse as before. ## Testing - `cd webui && bun run test` — 1118 tests passed - `cd webui && bun run build` - `cd webui && bun run lint` Regression coverage includes model normalization, pane removal, active-pane deletion, refresh restoration, legacy saved state, and unrelated-session fallback behavior.

records.title: NanoBot: fix: summarize persisted JSON tool results
records.content: ## Problem When an oversized tool result is persisted, nanobot currently uses the first 1,200 characters as the model-facing preview. If a large nested object appears first, useful root-level outcome fields such as `ok`, `status`, `error`, `artifact`, or `revision` can disappear from the preview even though they are needed for the next reasoning step. ## Change - Parse oversized JSON object and array results before rendering their preview. - Put bounded root-level scalar fields first and represent nested containers by shape only. - Bound long scalar values and the number of root fields. - Keep the complete persisted artifact unchanged. - Preserve the existing prefix preview for non-JSON results and scalar JSON values. This changes only the compact preview after the existing persistence threshold is crossed; it does not change tool execution or the stored full output. ## Validation - `pytest tests/agent/test_runner_persistence.py -q` — 8 passed - `ruff check nanobot/utils/helpers.py tests/agent/test_runner_persistence.py` - `git diff --check` Regression coverage verifies that root success/failure metadata remains visible while large nested content stays out of the preview and remains intact in the persisted file.

records.title: NanoBot: fix(agent): stop discarded sessions from reviving
records.content: ## Problem When a session is discarded, its active Agent task is cancelled and the session cache is invalidated. However, messages that were already waiting in the session's pending queue or deferred automation queue could still be published to the global message bus during task cleanup. Those messages were then processed as new inbound messages. Since `SessionManager.invalidate()` only removes the cached session and does not permanently mark the session key as discarded, the message routing path could recreate the session and start a new Agent task. As a result, a discarded session could be revived in the background and continue to: - consume LLM tokens; - execute tools or subprocesses; - run deferred cron/local-trigger tasks; - produce unexpected side effects. ## Root Cause The discard lifecycle and normal turn cleanup shared the same finalization logic. Normal turn cleanup is expected to republish messages: ```text normal turn finishes → republish pending messages → publish the next deferred automation turn But discard cleanup should have different semantics: session is discarded → cancel active work → drop pending messages → cancel deferred automation → do not publish anything for this session The existing implementation only checked _discarding_sessions to skip runtime checkpoint restoration after cancellation. It did not apply the same discard guard to the finally block, which still: - republished pending queue leftovers; - published the next deferred automation turn. In addition, deferred automation waiters had no explicit session-level termination path, so simply removing deferred messages could leave cron/local-trigger callers waiting indefinitely. ``` ## Solution Implement a session-scoped discard fence while preserving the existing normal-turn behavior. ### Automation coordinator cleanup Add session-level discard handling to AutomationTurnCoordinator: - remove deferred automation messages for the discarded session; - complete in-flight automation waiters

records.title: NanoBot: fix(tui): preserve cursor position on Windows exit
records.content: ## Summary Prevent the TUI from returning the shell cursor to terminal history after `nanobot agent` exits in affected Windows terminals. The fix disables OpenTUI's explicit-width capability probe by default on Windows while preserving explicit user overrides. ## Problem In some embedded Windows terminals, exiting `nanobot agent` returns control to PowerShell with the cursor positioned inside the existing terminal history instead of below the TUI. This can cause: - the PowerShell prompt to remain invisible until Enter is pressed; - the cursor to appear over previous commands; - existing terminal output to look overwritten or rearranged. The issue is caused by OpenTUI's OSC 66 explicit-width capability probe. The probe runs on the primary screen before the renderer becomes active and relies on cursor save/restore behavior that is not handled correctly by the affected terminal. Upgrading from OpenTUI 0.5.3 to 0.5.4 did not resolve the issue. An A/B test confirmed that disabling this probe restores the expected cursor position. ## Changes - Configure the OpenTUI environment before creating the renderer. - Default `OPENTUI_FORCE_EXPLICIT_WIDTH` to `false` on Windows. - Preserve an explicitly configured `OPENTUI_FORCE_EXPLICIT_WIDTH` value. - Leave behavior on Linux and macOS unchanged. - Add tests for the Windows default, explicit overrides, and non-Windows behavior. - Keep OpenTUI pinned to version 0.5.3, and this PR does not change dependencies. ## Tests - `bun run check` - `bun run test` — 163 tests passed - Windows ConPTY smoke test - Manual A/B test in an embedded Windows PowerShell terminal - Manual test with all related environment variables removed ## Visual comparison Both recordings use the same Windows PowerShell terminal, terminal dimensions, command, and TUI exit method. ### Before [<!-- The before-fix video -->](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef5c7b18-25d9-424e-9757-6b676e678e37) After the TUI exits, the cursor returns to a previous line in the

records.title: NanoBot: refactor(providers): make fallback attempts explicit
records.content: ## Summary - introduce an immutable `ProviderAttempt` and an explicit async route that resolves the concrete provider, model, transport, context window, continuation mode, native-compaction capability, and retry policy before execution - make `AgentRunner` drive that route from one unchanged source transcript, so transient retries stay inside one attempt while provider/model/transport/capability fallbacks yield a new attempt - express fallback-provider routing and OpenAI Responses -> native-disabled Responses -> Chat Completions routing through the same attempt contract, including Azure Responses and OpenAI Codex native-compaction compatibility fallback - preserve direct provider calls, per-leaf retries, circuit breaking, streaming recovery, continuation checks, fallback notifications, and terminal retry events ## Why this is a prerequisite NAN-67 needs Runner to fit a request for the provider call that will actually execute. Today, provider/model/transport fallback can change that identity below Runner. Injecting a request-fit callback into those lower layers creates bidirectional control flow and makes the final compaction strategy implicit. This PR changes only routing: Runner first receives a concrete attempt, and NAN-67 can later fit the original transcript once for that attempt. If routing advances, the next attempt is fitted again from the same source rather than from a request copy mutated for the previous attempt. ## Behavioral contract - transient retry: same `ProviderAttempt` - provider, model, transport, or native-capability fallback: new `ProviderAttempt` - Responses -> Chat: rebuild continuation, matching current behavior - compatible Responses/native fallback: retain continuation when the leaf can resume it - streamed non-timeout errors: do not fail over after emitted content - streamed timeout recovery: preserve the existing segment/recovery rules ## Non-goals - no native/local request-fit or context-compaction policy - no Memory/Dream consolidation,

records.title: NanoBot: refactor(agent): extract tool execution boundary

After this change, those responsibilities belong to `tools.execution`; the runner calls one `execute_tool_calls(...)` function and retains only the decision of when the ReAct loop enters the tool phase. No public Tool, Hook, provider, or runner result contract changes are intended. ## Verification - `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/agent/test_runner_tool_execution.py tests/agent/tools/test_subagent_tools.py -q` — 29 passed - `uv run --no-sync ruff check tests/agent/tools/test_subagent_tools.py` - changed-file BasedPyright — 0 errors, 0 warnings - `git diff --check` Related: [NAN-17](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-17/长期架构治理让-nanobot-重新小而清晰)
